NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Friday postponed its proposed ‘public impeachment’ proceedings against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to Saturday due to rain. Article Title: Night polo goesmainstream in Jaipur
Article Text:
A night polo match underway at the Rambagh Polo Club ground in Jaipur

An Evening At The Polo

In this bastion of the ‘sport of kings’, horse and rider are routinely taking to the field under floodlights, in the hope of drawing a wider audience, building tourism opportunities — and preserving a bit of the city’s heritage, writes Mandakini Shaly

A Place In The City

Finding Players And Spectators

Later Dinners For The Horses

Polo in Jaipur has become easier to catch. Matches at the Rambagh Polo Club ground now begin at 7.30pm, giving office-goers time to get there after work and families a chance to watch once the daytime heat has passed.Over the past couple of months, 10 newly installed floodlights have lit up the ground near the Vidhan Sabha and the high court. In a neighbourhood where lights over the Sawai Man Singh Stadium have long signalled IPL season, there is now another reason to stop for a match.The stands have young spectators watching their first game, taking selfies and discovering a sport whose familiar audience has largely been drawn from royal families, the cavalry and club circles. Broad-brimmed hats, pastel linen jackets and chiffon sarees are still in evidence. The club is hoping to give more people a reason to come.Night polo has been played in Hyderabad and Noida, in smaller arenas with sand surfaces. Jaipur’s matches are on a full-sized grass ground, under lights, as part of the official tournament schedule.For Major Anant Rajpurohit of 61 Cavalry, a veteran player, the advantage is straightforward: more people are free to watch.“The good point is that people tend to get off from work, office, or day commitments, and the attendance is more,” he says.“Earlier, the matches and all the finals were done during the daytime, so the availability of gentlemen and ladies was very restricted and very confined. The development of any sport comes when the number of people watching it is more. Then, the number of people who intend to get into the sport or invest into the sport increases. So that way it is an added advantage,” he says.For Padmanabh Singh, 28, India’s polo captain and scion of the erstwhile Jaipur royal family, encouraging people to watch is also part of keeping a city tradition alive.“I have always viewed polo as very intertwined with the culture of Jaipur,” he says. “Jaipur is one of the main hubs of polo across the world and has given a lot to the sport. Some of the most iconic moments have happened here. So when I talk about conservation, restoration, and preservation of our culture and heritage, I mean polo too. It’s part of our tourism.”Rambagh Polo Club is marketing the sport more actively, with support from Rajasthan’s tourism leadership. Padmanabh’s mother, Diya Kumari, is deputy chief minister and tourism minister.Last month, a UAE delegation visited Jaipur to discuss cooperation in polo, horses and tourism. Among its interests was the Marwari, Rajasthan’s indigenous horse breed.“The Marwari is our local breed here in Rajasthan, and the visiting delegation was incredibly keen to see them. We discussed avenues to encourage a vibrant cultural exchange between the UAE, Rajasthan Tourism, and Rambagh Polo Club. They are very eager to support polo further and bring global visibility to this magnificent breed that has served Rajasthan for centuries,” Padmanabh says.Elsewhere, access to a convenient ground is a concern. Delhi, Maharashtra and West Bengal have active polo circuits, supported by the Army, professional players and corporate patrons. In Delhi, however, Rajpurohit worries that a change of venue will cost the sport spectators and sponsors.“The finals of all elite tournaments in Delhi used to be at Jaipur Polo Ground, which is in the heart of Delhi,” he says. “Unfortunately, we lost that ground a few months back. Now more matches will be conducted at the Army Polo and Riding Centre. It is a shame that we lost the ground in the heart of Delhi. The number of people who used to attend and sponsor the events were more. Now that number will reduce.”He sees encouraging signs in the number of younger players taking up the sport.“The number of horses that have been shipped in every year is increasing. The number of kids who intend to compete in the sport is increasing. Earlier we used to have around four odd teams in Junior National Championship. Now we have six-seven teams,” he adds.Polo remains expensive to take up, though schools are helping introduce children to it.“There are many schools that are offering the equestrian part and the polo part, like Mayo and Delhi College, and they are coming up very well.”In Jaipur, demand for lessons already exceeds what the Sawai Man Singh Polo School and Academy can offer.“With that spirit in mind, a few years ago we started the Sawai Man Singh Polo School and Academy. It’s the only one of its kind and it’s doing very well. We have 50 students, which is our maximum capacity, and for the last three years, we have had a waiting list,” Padmanabh says.“Unfortunately, we can’t accommodate more because we have a limited number of horses, but it’s in the heart of the city and subsidised by the polo club. I donated some of my horses to the academy and I go there all the time to mentor them. Whenever someone is doing well, I pull them out to play with us,” Padmanabh says.Padmanabh says Jaipur’s experience of playing after dark goes back more than a century. He describes a brass night polo ball, with a small candle inside, used by women who played at night.At Rambagh, playing under floodlights requires a change in the horses’ routine. Matches fall at what would ordinarily be their dinner time.“I would not say that it changes much. We just have to adjust the feeding time. Now, they have to have dinner a little bit later. So we just have to adapt our schedules,” Padmanabh says.The horses, he says, have settled into the later hours without trouble.“We know that if the horse is not happy, it won’t eat, or it will stop drinking water, or it will stop laying down. None of that happens. In fact, it is better for them because they don’t have the heat of the day.”
Article Summary: Polo in Jaipur has become easier to catch. Matches at the Rambagh Polo Club ground now begin at 7.30pm. 10 newly installed floodlights have lit up the ground near the Vidhan Sabha. Padmanabh Singh, 28, India’s polo captain, says it is part of a city tradition.

Article Title: Firecracker ban: No point in passing orders without enforcement, says SC
Article Text:
SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it was not inclined to completely ban firecrackers, but there was no point in passing orders and directions every year unless authorities implement them on the ground.“It concerns every living being,” a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale observed while hearing a matter on the bursting of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR.Additional solicitor-general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench about the measures taken by Delhi govt and Commission for Air Quality Management to deal with air pollution.“There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.While saying that it was not an adversarial matter, the bench observed that authorities have to take up the issue seriously and take action. “You have to really regulate it. Every year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it can’t be done,” it said.“We also understand the sentiments of the public. We are not inclined to completely ban, but don’t push us to take a very harsh stand,” the bench told Bhati.Bhati said a series of measures have been taken which would come into effect from Nov, including curbs on older vehicles, construction and demolition activity and staggered office timings in Delhi. “We are geared up to deal with the pollution season which unfortunately happens,” she said.Centre also told the bench that its internal consultation on the issue pertaining to the use of barium in firecrackers was going on. Bhati requested the bench to grant three weeks to complete the consultation.The top court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case concerning air pollution in NCR covering issues like firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. The other plea relates to a ban on manufacturing firecrackers.During the hearing, an advocate, assisting the apex court as an amicus curiae in the suo motu case, said bursting firecrackers releases a huge amount of hazardous particulate matter (PM) which enters the human body and causes damage to lungs and other organs.She said during Dussehra last week, there was a spike in the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Delhi-NCR. Flagging the issue of enforcement, the amicus said there was no proper mechanism to assess whether the firecrackers which are being sold are actually green crackers.The bench had said that a middle ground would have to be found by specifying hours during which firecrackers could be used.
Article Summary: SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement. “There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.

Article Title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
Article Text:
BJP's big win in MLC elections comes with setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi

BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra.

BJP mocks Congress over 'zero' seats

BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted Congress over its poor performance in the MLC elections, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers.

Nagpur win gives Congress a chance to respond

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the BJP's setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi after PM Modi mocked the party's performance in the MLC elections.

Varanasi setback gives SP a boost ahead of 2027

What do the results mean for 2027?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The MLC elections across four states brought both shock and cheer for the BJP and Congress. While the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in Karnataka, where it is in power but failed to win a single seat, the BJP faltered in two constituencies which mattered the most. One being Nagpur, which is home to the RSS headquarters, and Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency.The BJP nevertheless emerged as the largest party, winning 13 of the 28 seats contested, while its allies took the NDA's tally to 16. The alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, won six of the 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh and secured four of the eight seats in Bihar. In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two of the five seats, while the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi secured three.The Congress's only victory came from Nagpur, a political stronghold of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari. In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party retained the Varanasi Teachers' constituency and was heading towards victory in the Graduates' seat, both of which it had won in 2020.What began as celebrations and sharp jibes at the Congress on Wednesday turned into a war of words on Thursday, as the results in Nagpur and Varanasi gave the opposition grounds to question the BJP's claims of electoral dominance.As the early results came in on Wednesday, BJP leaders targeted the Congress over its poor performance, particularly in Karnataka, where the party is in power but failed to win a single seat.PM Modi took a swipe at the opposition party on X, pointing out that voting in the four states had taken place using ballot papers."Guess how many seats Congress won?" he asked.The remark came amid the Congress's repeated allegations over electronic voting machines and its demand for a return to ballot-paper voting.BJP president Nitin Nabin also targeted the Congress, saying the party had failed to win public support despite voting being conducted using ballot papers."The people are repeatedly rejecting Congress' anarchist politics," Nabin said, adding that public trust remained with PM Modi irrespective of whether elections were conducted using EVMs or ballot papers.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also attacked Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of vote theft"Kamchori ki aadat chhodiye. Vote chori ka shabd apke muh se khud chhoot jayega," he said, asking the Congress leader to give up what he described as a habit of avoiding hard work.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency after more than 40 hours of counting.Kohale had initially taken the lead before Wanjari overtook him through preferential votes.Nagpur is important for the BJP. Besides housing the RSS headquarters, it is associated with Fadnavis and Gadkari, both of whom campaigned for Kohale.The Congress had wrested the seat from the BJP in 2020, when Wanjari defeated Sandip Joshi. By retaining it in 2026, the party prevented the BJP from reclaiming a constituency it had dominated for decades.The Maharashtra Congress also targeted Fadnavis over a social media post in which he had claimed that the party had failed to win a single seat.Sharing a screenshot of what it said was a deleted post by Fadnavis, the party accused him of celebrating before counting was complete. The post had described the Congress's performance as a "big fat zero".The Congress said Fadnavis had been forced to delete the post after the Nagpur result and warned that the outcome was only a trailer of future political battles.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh also responded to PM Modi's remarks, questioning the BJP's losses in Nagpur and Varanasi."The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's lecturing others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?" Ramesh said."Mr. Modi, stop the trolling," he added, accusing the government of failing to address inflation, unemployment and weak private investment.Ramesh claimed that voters in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had expressed dissatisfaction with the Centre's policies.The BJP's biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh came from Varanasi, where the Samajwadi Party retained the Teachers' seat and established an unassailable lead in the Graduates' constituency.The BJP retained six of the 11 seats contested in the state, while the SP won four and was heading towards a fifth.The SP had won both Varanasi seats in 2020 as well. Six years later, the BJP has failed to dislodge the party from either constituency despite its strong presence in the region.Although the two MLC constituencies cover a wider geographical area than PM Modi's Lok Sabha seat, the results carry political significance given Varanasi's association with the Prime Minister since 2014.They also come after PM Modi's victory margin in Varanasi declined from nearly 4.8 lakh votes in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to around 1.5 lakh in 2024.Across Uttar Pradesh, the SP's tally is set to rise from three seats in 2020 to five, while the BJP has retained its tally of six.The SP had also emerged as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, winning 37 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats against the BJP's 33.BJP deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya acknowledged that the party had expected a better performance."These elections are decided by highly educated and qualified voters. The BJP has repeated its previous performance, but we expected to win more seats. We will examine why we fell short," Maurya said.The SP, meanwhile, has repeatedly accused the BJP of electoral irregularities, allegations the ruling party has rejected.On polling day, Akhilesh Yadav had claimed that the BJP was attempting to influence even the MLC elections, which have a limited electorate."If the BJP can do this in MLC polls for teachers and graduate constituencies where a limited number of people cast votes, one can imagine their preparation for the assembly polls," he had said.The NDA's overall tally shows that the BJP and its allies remain ahead in these Legislative Council contests. But the results in Nagpur and Varanasi also show that the party has struggled to regain certain seats despite its strong presence in both regions.In Uttar Pradesh, the SP and Congress are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections together, hoping to build on their performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.The alliance won 43 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats in 2024, reducing the BJP's tally from 62 in 2019 to 33. Akhilesh Yadav has said the alliance will continue in 2027, although the two parties still need to settle their seat-sharing arrangement.The MLC results, however, cannot be treated as an indication of how the state will vote in the assembly elections. These contests involve a limited electorate of registered graduates and teachers, unlike assembly polls, which are decided by a much wider voter base.For the BJP, which is seeking a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, the challenge will be to counter the opposition's gains. For the SP-Congress alliance, the question is whether it can repeat its 2024 Lok Sabha performance when the state's 403 assembly seats go to the polls in 2027.
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra. PM Modi mocked Congress over its poor performance, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers.

Article Title: Bihar Museum in world top 10, ahead of Met, Louvre
Article Text:
Image Source: WikiMedia Commons

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Artist Subodh Gupta helped put Bihar on the global art map with his signature bartan sculptures.Even so, the art world was surprised to see the barely decade-old Bihar Museum ranked ninth on the 'World's 100 Best Museums 2026' list, ahead of institutions such as New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Louvre in Paris.Published by Munich-based travel publication Worth a Journey, the list ranks the Patna institution as No. 1 in Asia.It is the only Indian museum in the top 100. The rankings draw on visitor reviews, data analytics and on-site expert evaluations.The museum may not have the Mona Lisa, but it has a crown jewel of its own: the Didarganj Yakshi.Carved from a single block of highly polished Chunar sandstone, the 2,000-year-old, life-sized statue stands in an air-conditioned room. Her nose is chipped and her left arm broken, but she seems ready to swat away any obstacle with the fly-whisk (chauri) in her hand.Beyond the Yakshi, the 13.9-acre complex houses the famed Kurkihar bronzes, prehistoric stone tools and a Kushan-period 'Birth of the Buddha' slab. The museum building, designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki and Studio Opolis, an architectural practice located in Mumbai and Pune, is quite striking too.On X, industrialist Anand Mahindra called it "a seminal moment of recognition", adding that it has the potential to be a game changer for the museum-going experience in India.
Article Summary: Bihar Museum ranked ninth on the 'World's 100 Best Museums 2026' list. It is the only Indian museum in the top 100. The Patna institution houses the Didarganj Yakshi, a 2,000-year-old, life-sized statue.

Article Title: MLC poll setback opens new front within Mahayuti; Shinde-for-CM pitch, 'Shakuni mama' jibe fly
Article Text:

'Shakuni mamas in Mahayuti should be identified'

NEW DELHI: Cracks within Maharashtra's ruling Mahayuti alliance came out in the open on Thursday after a Shiv Sena leader advocated for deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde to be elevated to the post of chief minister.Speaking to reporters after the MLC election results, former MLA Ravindra Dhangekar said the outcome reflected people's views of the Devendra Fadnavis-led government."When there are doubts about the state government's image, such results are a reflection of it," Dhangekar said."When Eknath Shinde was chief minister, he helped Mahayuti come to power. Shinde should again become chief minister," he added.Dhangekar's remarks were quickly rebuked by the BJP, which said the Shiv Sena leader had no authority to comment on the issue."Out of 149 contested seats (in the 2024 assembly elections), BJP won 137," senior BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said.MLC Pravin Darekar also lashed out at Dhangekar and advised him to "stay within his limits"."The state is progressing like never before under Fadnavis's leadership. He hates Fadnavis so much that he never misses an opportunity to criticise him," the BJP leader said."We never made any comment against your leadership and will never do so.We will not tolerate your attempts to tarnish Fadnavis's image," Darekar added.The remarks came after the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi won three of the five graduates' and teachers' constituencies of the legislative council that went to the polls on October 23. Meanwhile, Mahayuti bagged two seats.Meanwhile, BJP leader and Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane called for identifying "Shakuni mamas" within the ruling Mahayuti alliance after its lacklustre performance in the MLC elections."It is time to find out whether there are any 'Shakuni mamas' within Mahayuti who follow the scripts that Uddhav Thackeray likes," he said.Shakuni is a character in the Mahabharata known for creating discord and plotting against others.Rane said the ruling alliance had not achieved the expected success, but the BJP had still won two seats in constituencies it had not contested in the previous election."We fought as one force in the assembly elections, taking up the Hindutva agenda, and the results were evident. Our allies must understand the strength of Mahayuti," he said."Our candidate was ahead by 4,500 votes in the first-preference count. The Congress candidate won because of Nitesh Karale's second-preference votes. The Congress should thank Karale," he said.
Article Summary: 'Shakuni mamas in Mahayuti should be identified,' says BJP leader. Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Dhangekar calls for deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde to be elevated to the post of chief minister. Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi won three of the five graduates' and teachers' constituencies.

Article Title: SIR deadlines extended in 5 states, Delhi; EC sets new dates for final rolls
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India has revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Delhi, extending the deadline for final publication of voter lists.According to separate letters issued by the commission on October 29, the final electoral rolls for Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra will be published on November 30. For Delhi, the final publication has been pushed to December 22.The notice and claims-and-objections phase has also been extended, with revised deadlines varying by state. In Delhi, the period for filing claims and objections runs until November 25, while the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue until December 15.In Maharashtra, the claims-and-objections phase will run until November 25, while the period for filing claims and objections ends on November 13. In Nagaland, the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue until November 25. Haryana’s corresponding phase has been extended until November 20, while Telangana’s will continue until November 26.The commission has directed the officials concerned to publicise the revised schedules and inform political parties in writing.
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India has revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Final electoral rolls for Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra will be published on November 30. For Delhi, the final publication has been pushed to December 22.

Article Title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar shrugged off the legislative council election results after the Samajwadi Party defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency, saying the election reflected the mandate of educated voters rather than the general electorate.Speaking to reporters, Rajbhar said the MLC elections had no connection with the assembly elections.“This is the people’s mandate, the mandate of educated voters, and we welcome the verdict,” Rajbhar said.“However, these elections have no connection with the assembly elections. Historically, educated voters often do not turn up to vote in assembly elections and instead treat the day as a holiday,” he added.The BJP won six seats and the Samajwadi Party won five of the 11 seats in the biennial elections. The results come months ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, widely seen as a test of popularity between the BJP and the SP.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav described the BJP's performance in the MLC elections as a "double defeat" and said the results had laid the groundwork for his party's victory in the assembly polls.In a post on X, Akhilesh said the BJP lost the Varanasi Graduates' constituency in both the initial count and the recount, calling it a "double defeat of the double engine government".The SP chief said the BJP's defeat "was the defeat of its policies concerning teachers, students and education" and that "the educated unemployed graduates had also delivered their verdict" against the party.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency. NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday called the BJP a “flop show” after the party's defeat in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections. He also claimed the results set the stage for the 2027 UP assembly polls.In a post on X, Akhilesh credited teachers and young voters for the victory and alleged that the BJP had tampered with election results.“The BJP's defeat in the Legislative Council elections has written the preface to the UP assembly elections to be held in 2027,” he said.Akhilesh also claimed that the BJP had lost in Varanasi during both the initial counting and the subsequent recounting. He described the outcome as a “double loss of the double engine”, referring to the BJP's governments at the Centre and in the state.He alleged that the results reflected public anger against the BJP's policies on teachers, students and education, as well as the concerns of unemployed graduates.“The BJP's ticket window is empty,” Akhilesh said, claiming that the ruling party was struggling to find candidates for the 2027 Assembly elections. He further alleged that the BJP was facing an internal rift following its defeat in the council polls.Akhilesh also claimed that the PDA, or Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) grouping, had expanded its support base.“The PDA's mass base has now reached 95%, because 'those who are victimized, they are PDA'!” he said.The SP chief alleged that the BJP had won some seats through electoral manipulation. He also praised party workers and supporters for monitoring the counting process alongside the party's “PDA sentinels”.He congratulated the winning candidates and those who, he alleged, had been defeated through “deceit and fraud”.“In fact, none of our candidates has lost; they just couldn't win in the face of BJP's tampering. We equally honor them as well. For us, they are all winners even without certificates,” Akhilesh said.He thanked teachers and young voters for supporting the party and remaining vigilant until the winning candidates received their certificates.“This very vigilance and unity will become the 'decisive foundation' for forming our government in 2027,” he said.The Samajwadi Party also shared a list of its winning candidates in the graduate and teachers' constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections.The candidates named in the post were Kanti Singh from the Lucknow graduate constituency, Lal Bihari Yadav from the Varanasi teachers' constituency, Akash Agrawal from the Agra teachers' constituency, Ashutosh Sinha from the Varanasi graduate constituency, and Man Singh Yadav from the Jhansi-Prayagraj graduate constituency.The party congratulated the candidates and described their victories as a morale boost ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav called the BJP a ‘flop show’ after the party's defeat in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections. He also claimed the results set the stage for the 2027 UP assembly polls. Akhilesh credited teachers and young voters for the victory and alleged that the BJP had tampered with election results.

Article Title: A vitamin clue to stroke in the young? Bengaluru study finds low B6 levels
Article Text:
Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Clinica Chimica Acta

NEW DELHI: A vitamin that helps the body process proteins and regulate important chemical reactions may offer a new clue to why young adults suffer strokes. A study by researchers in Bengaluru has found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke than in healthy people of a similar age.Ahead of World Stroke Day on October 29, the findings draw attention to a possible factor associated with stroke in young adults. The study compared 171 young adults who had suffered an ischaemic stroke, caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain, with 249 healthy controls.Median vitamin B6 levels in stroke patients were 40.9 nmol/L, compared with 65.6 nmol/L in the control group. Vitamin B6 insufficiency, defined by the researchers as levels below 30 nmol/L, was found in 12.3% of stroke patients, compared with just 0.7% of healthy controls.Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.Prof Manjari Tripathi, head of the department of neurology at AIIMS, said vitamin B6 is essential for homocysteine metabolism. “Low vitamin B6 levels can impair this process, allowing homocysteine to rise. Elevated homocysteine can damage blood vessels, promote inflammation and contribute to clot formation, increasing stroke risk.Maintaining adequate vitamin B6 levels through a balanced diet is important,” she said.The Bengaluru study adds to evidence linking vitamin B6 levels with stroke risk, but whether improving these levels can prevent strokes remains unclear. Dr Pravin Gupta, chairman, Marengo Asia international institute of neuro and spine, said the study was significant because vitamin B6 levels can be measured through a blood test. “However, this study shows an association, not proof that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke. Further research is needed,” he said.The researchers, led by scientists from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, found that lower vitamin B6 levels were independently associated with higher odds of ischaemic stroke even after accounting for other factors. Among stroke patients, vitamin B6 levels were strongly inversely correlated with homocysteine, an amino acid associated with blood vessel health.Published inin 2026, the case-control study adds to research into factors associated with stroke among younger adults. However, it cannot establish whether low vitamin B6 contributes to stroke, results from other health or dietary factors, or reflects an underlying process. Further studies are needed to validate the findings.The results do not establish that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke or that routine testing for the vitamin should be recommended for young adults.
Article Summary: Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach. Researchers in Bengaluru found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Roman Reigns inspired his punches; Andre Russell earned him a nickname: Meet Army havaldar and Asian Games medallist Kapil Pokhariya
Article Text:
Kapil Pokhariya's fascination with pro-wrestler Roman Reigns was well known in his locality. (Image credit: Special arrangement)

From Khatima to the Asian Games podium

Kapil Pokhariya with his father (Image credit: Special arrangement)

From a small training ground to the boxing ring

Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)

Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)

The ‘ Andre Russell ’ of Khatima

Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)

The Road Ahead and LA 2028 Dream

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jumping on cotton-filled mattresses, punching pillows, throwing them over walls and hitting a homemade punching bag filled with mountain soil - Kapil Pokhariya’s childhood was all about pro-wrestling.His fascination with pro-wrestler Roman Reigns was well known in his locality. He would skip meals, playtime, and outings to watch WWE programming on television. Once the show was over, he would try to copy the moves and punches at home.Little did he know that this childhood fascination could one day bring him his biggest recognition.Today, Kapil - an Indian Army havaldar - is an Asian Games medallist. Kapil won bronze in the men’s 90kg boxing event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.“I never knew that copying Roman Reigns and practising those punches would bring me this far. I used to save recordings of his videos, and I still have them. I am really proud of where I am today. Honestly, I started learning how to throw punches by copying Roman Reigns (laugh),” Kapil told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview."My favourite was WrestleMania and Money in the Bank," he said.Kapil hails from Chakarpur village in Khatima, Uttarakhand, far from the major boxing centres that have produced several Indian stars.His father, Narendra Singh Pokhariya, served in the Indian Army. He wanted his son to study well and join the Army as a commissioned officer. Boxing, however, was never part of the original plan.Narendra often watched his son copy WWE stars at home. Initially, he would scold and even beat him for damaging things around the house. But his view slowly changed when he saw Kapil putting sand into a thick sack after returning from school and punching it with all his strength.“A teacher used to teach boxing at a nearby school. I saw the students punching a bag and decided to make one myself. My father scolded me in the beginning, but later he took me to a training centre and got me admitted there. That is how I got into boxing,” Kapil said.Kapil did not begin his boxing journey at a big academy. His first steps came at a small training ground, where he practised alongside boys of his age and those who were older. After a few months, he began training under a coach.“I come from a small village where boxing was never a popular sport. Pooran Bohra sir was there. He trained a small group of boys for just a few hours on selected days of the week. But I was interested in learning. I listened to him carefully and repeated everything he taught me when I returned home,” Kapil said.With time, Kapil developed as a boxer and competed in his first state-level competition in 2015. He went into the tournament with excitement but came away disappointed. His first competitive bout ended in defeat in the opening round.“I was really disappointed. It was the first bout of my life, and I was seeing such a large crowd for the first time. I lost in the first round. But that competition and the defeat taught me a lot. My interest in boxing grew even stronger after that,” he said.Kapil returned with a different mindset at the national-level competition. This time, he did more than win his bouts - he also claimed the gold medal. The prize money was followed by a job in the Indian Army. He joined the force in April 2017 and was appointed as a havaldar. His boxing career took a big step forward after that.The Army gave him opportunities to improve his skills and compete at a higher level. He began training more seriously, took part in Services competitions, won medals and continued to grow as a boxer.“My father wanted me to study and join the Army as a commissioned officer. He joined as a sepoy and retired as a havaldar. But he wanted me to reach a higher rank if I joined the Indian Army,” Kapil said.“He was very happy. The day I won a national medal, he hugged me. That was when I realised that I had achieved something big in my life,” Kapil said.“Now, after winning this Asian Games medal, I will be promoted to naib subedar. Papa said, ‘Ab tu mera senior ho gaya hai’,” the Indian boxer recalled with a smile.Like many children in India, Kapil also grew up playing gully cricket. He even played inter-village cricket in Uttarakhand.His height, muscular build and powerful hitting made him a popular figure on the local cricket grounds. His ability to hit big sixes earned him the nickname ‘Russell’, after West Indies power-hitter Andre Russell.“I loved Andre Russell. I also liked Hardik Pandya. People used to call me ‘Khatima ka Russell’ because of my power. The boys wanted me in their team because I could hit big sixes,” he said, laughing.For Kapil, the Asian Games bronze is only the beginning. His biggest dream is to represent India at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and win a medal.Under the Boxing Federation of India's selection criteria, Asian Games medallists will be selected as the main entries in their respective weight categories for the 2027 World Boxing Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. The tournament is scheduled for April and will be the first qualifying event in boxing for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.Kapil knows there is still a long road ahead. “Rukna nahi hai ab, bas aage dekhna hai,” he said.“The Olympics is the ultimate dream. I want to go there, represent my country and win a medal. That is the only thing on my mind right now. I am preparing for the World Championships in April,” he added.
Article Summary: Kapil Pokhariya won bronze in the men’s 90kg boxing event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Kapil hails from Chakarpur village in Khatima, Uttarakhand, far from the major boxing centres that have produced several Indian stars. His fascination with pro-wrestler Roman Reigns was well known in his locality.

Article Title: Tom Brady's charity work spans $46.5 million, African poverty relief and sick children's wishes
Article Text:
Tom Brady (Getty Images)

Tom Brady's charity work supports people with disabilities and global communities

Tom Brady's TB12 Foundation and Make-A-Wish support athletes and children

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady built his name on record-breaking performances and six Super Bowl victories with the New England Patriots. Yet his influence has reached far beyond the football field. The NFL legend has used his fame, time and resources to support people facing challenges that often go unnoticed. From helping athletes access healthcare to supporting children with serious illnesses, Brady has backed causes that aim to create lasting change. His charitable work also reaches communities in Africa, where an eye-opening visit helped shape his understanding of global poverty and the need for greater support.One of Brady's most significant charitable commitments has been to Best Buddies International, a nonprofit that helps people with intellectual and developmental disabilities build friendships, find jobs and become more involved in their communities.According to Borgen Magazine, Brady helped raise $46.5 million for the organisation over two decades. He also served as an honorary co-chair of its annual cycling, running and walking event for 16 years before becoming a global ambassador in December 2019.His involvement went beyond fundraising, with appearances at events helping bring attention to the organisation's mission.Brady also turned his attention to poverty in Africa. In 2004, he travelled to Ghana and Uganda with Debt, AIDS, Trade, Africa (DATA), an organisation that worked to raise awareness of poverty and development issues across the continent.During the trip, he visited schools, medical clinics and an HIV/AIDS clinic in Uganda that received support from US foreign aid. Seeing the challenges faced by local communities gave him a closer look at how international assistance could make a difference.Reflecting on the experience, Brady said, “I saw the best and brightest of the human spirit in the face of incredible poverty that most of us just can’t comprehend. When you see what CAN be done, it’s impossible to not be driven to do more — the needs are still overwhelming.”His words highlighted the gap between the resources available in wealthier countries and the urgent needs facing vulnerable communities.Brady also established a charitable initiative of his own. In 2015, he founded the TB12 Foundation to help athletes pursue their performance goals by improving access to health and wellness resources.The foundation focused on people from low-income backgrounds and athletes who might otherwise struggle to afford the support they needed. Its fundraising efforts included an annual marathon in Boston, which raised more than $125,000 in the year cited by Borgen Magazine to help provide healthcare resources.Brady has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, which creates memorable experiences for children living with serious illnesses. In 2019, he and his New England Patriots teammates welcomed five children, showed them around the team's stadium and treated them to dinner.These efforts reveal another side of Brady's public life. His charitable work has combined financial contributions with personal involvement, helping organisations reach people who need support. While his football achievements remain central to his legacy, his work beyond the game shows how an athlete's platform can also draw attention to disability inclusion, healthcare access and global poverty.
Article Summary: NFL legend has used his fame, time and resources to support people facing challenges that often go unnoticed. He has helped raise $46.5 million for Best Buddies International over two decades. Brady has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, which creates memorable experiences for children living with serious illnesses.

Article Title: "I am in tears for such a gift": Travis Kelce's $2 million gift brings hope to families of fallen NYPD officers and firefighters

Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift donate $2 million to Answer The Call

Travis Kelce’s wedding donation brings comfort to families of fallen first responders

In July 2026, Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift made a charitable contribution that reached far beyond their high-profile wedding celebrations. The couple donated $2 million to Answer The Call, a New York nonprofit that supports families of first responders killed in the line of duty. The gift moved families who have spent years coping with loss, offering financial support and a reminder that their loved ones have not been forgotten. For Kelce, the donation also put the spotlight on how public figures can use major life milestones to support people facing challenges that extend well beyond the sporting world.The donation formed part of a wider charitable effort by the newlyweds, who reportedly contributed a combined $26 million to organisations across the United States during their wedding week. Their $2 million gift to Answer The Call stood out for its direct connection to families who lost loved ones while serving New York City.Founded in 1985, Answer The Call provides immediate financial assistance and ongoing stipends to the families of fallen New York City police officers, firefighters, Port Authority police officers and emergency medical services personnel.On July 20, the organisation thanked Kelce and Swift through an Instagram post featuring letters from nine recipients.Their messages showed how the support reaches beyond financial help, offering families comfort and recognition years after tragedy.Valerie Perry, whose husband, William, was a Port Authority police officer, described the lasting impact of the fund. He was shot and killed on December 22, 1980, and his family buried him on Christmas Eve.“Answer the Call has changed my life with our yearly checks, but they have also brought smiles because I feel like my Bill is always remembered, even after all these years,” she said.Perry also expressed her emotional response to the couple's contribution.“Now, to read about your donation? I am in tears for such a gift to all these families that have been through so much.“Prayers for your future together, and God bless both of you for your generosity and your caring souls for doing something so amazing.”The response from recipients highlighted the emotional weight of supporting families who continue to live with the loss of loved ones. For many, such contributions recognise not only their financial needs but also the sacrifices made by the people they lost.Theresa Giammona, whose husband, FDNY Captain Vincent Giammona, died in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, also thanked the couple. She recalled Swift performing at America’s Camp, a summer camp established for children who lost loved ones in the attacks.“My children have been devoted Taylor fans ever since they saw you perform at America’s Camp in 2003,” Giammona said. “What always meant the most to us is that you never forgot the America’s Camp families.”She added: “Thank you for Answering the Call, for your generosity, and most of all, for never forgetting the families you have continued to lift up over the years.”Answer The Call also praised Kelce and Swift for their support, saying: “Taylor and Travis, thank you for your incredible generosity and for standing with the families of fallen New York City first responders,” the organization said on Instagram. “Your gift will make a tangible difference in their lives.”The donation offered a meaningful example of how the couple's wedding celebrations could create opportunities to support others. While Kelce is best known for his NFL career, the contribution placed attention on a different side of his public life. For families who have endured decades of grief, the gift carried a message that their loved ones' service and sacrifice still matter.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift donated $2 million to Answer The Call. The New York nonprofit supports families of first responders killed in the line of duty. The donation was part of a wider charitable effort by the newlyweds. The couple reportedly contributed a combined $26 million to organisations.

Article Title: Nearly 75% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had this one condition
Article Text:
The Scary Truth About NFL Players’ Brain Health Revealed in New Study

JAMA Network Open

Scary NFL study reveals nearly 75% of deceased players had a devastating brain disease

Nearly 3 in 4 Former NFL Players Who Died Had CTE, New Study Uncovers

What is CTE, and why is it concerning? The study also examined dementia among former players

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new study has raised fresh concerns about the long-term effects of playing in the NFL. The study, published in, looked at 2,362 former NFL players who died during the 16-year period. Nearly 75% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts.Researchers from Boston University, Mass General Brigham and the Concussion & CTE Foundation worked together to estimate how common the disease was among the group. The findings are concerning because CTE has been linked to repeated blows to the head, something football players can experience throughout their careers. However, researchers stressed that the 74.5% figure is an estimate, not a confirmed diagnosis for every player included in the study.Of the former players included in the study, 387 had donated brains that were examined for CTE. Researchers found signs of the disease in 362 of them, or 93.5%. That is a very high percentage, but there is an important reason why the researchers did not use it as the final figure for all former NFL players.Families may be more likely to donate a player's brain if their loved one experienced memory problems, personality changes or other cognitive symptoms before death. This means that donated brains may not represent every former player who died during the same period.To account for this, the researchers examined additional records and adjusted their calculations to account for differences between players whose brains were donated and those whose brains were not. After making those adjustments, they estimated that 74.5% of all 2,362 deceased former players had CTE-related changes in their brains.Several famous NFL players have been diagnosed with CTE after death. Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez, who died in 2017 at age 27, was found to have Stage 3 CTE. Former San Diego Chargers linebacker Junior Seau, who died in 2012 at age 43, was also diagnosed with CTE after his death.Other notable cases include former Chicago Bears safety Dave Duerson, who died in 2011 at age 50, and former NFL quarterback Ken Stabler, who died in 2015 at age 69. Both were found to have CTE through postmortem brain examinations.Chronic traumatic encephalopathy, commonly known as CTE, is a progressive brain disease associated with repeated head impacts. It has been found in athletes who participated in contact sports, including American football.The disease is linked to an abnormal buildup of a protein called tau in the brain. Possible symptoms associated with CTE include memory loss, difficulty thinking, mood changes and problems with behavior or judgment. However, not everyone with CTE-related brain changes experiences the same symptoms. Some people may have relatively mild changes, while others may experience more serious problems.Another major challenge is that CTE can currently be confirmed only after death through an examination of brain tissue. Doctors cannot definitively diagnose the disease in a living person using routine medical tests. This also means researchers cannot use the new study to determine how many living NFL players currently have CTE.The researchers looked at dementia as a separate issue and estimated that 27.2% of the former NFL players had a history of dementia during their lifetime. Dementia can affect memory, thinking and a person's ability to manage everyday activities. However, it is not the same as CTE, and the two figures should not be confused.
Article Summary: Nearly 75% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts. Researchers found signs of the disease in 362 of them, or 93.5%. The 74.5% figure is an estimate, not a confirmed diagnosis for every player included in the study.

Article Title: How Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s donation helped a Nashville free grocery store resume support for families on its waitlist
Article Text:
An unexpected email

A $26 million charity donation

Pop icon Taylor Swift , 36, and NFL star Travis Kelce , 37, exchanged their wedding vows in July this year at Madison Square Garden. Ahead of their big day, the couple spent the week giving back. They donated $26 million to 20 charities, the Associated Press reported. One recipient was The Store, a Nashville non-profit fighting food insecurity. Rising food costs had forced the store to pause the admission of new families, and around 1,000 households were still waiting for help. That’s when an unexpected email arrived with a donation they simply couldn’t believe!Brittany Brown, The Store’s director of mission advancement, read the email twice before she believed it. It arrived in the days before Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in New York, a week when the couple’s names filled almost every feed. The message was not an invite. In fact, it had nothing to do with the wedding itself. It was about groceries, waiting lists and families who had been asked to be patient for months. Brown, whose job also involves explaining the non-profit’s work to donors and keeping the shelves stocked, quickly realised this was not routine support. “I quickly checked my email and was blown away, just really blown away,” Brown told Channel 5 Nashville.Country star Brad Paisley and actress Kimberly Williams-Paisley founded The Store, which opened in 2020. It works like a regular supermarket. Families referred to the store choose the food that fits their needs, with volunteers helping them shop. The store goes beyond traditional food aid and aims for longer-term solutions, according to its website.The donation arrived when The Store was struggling with rising grocery costs and had temporarily stopped accepting new families, leaving 1,000 households on its waiting list. Although Brown did not disclose the amount donated, she said the money would allow the organisation to begin admitting families again. “With this gift, we’re now going to be able to unpause that pause,” Brown told the broadcaster.In a video shared on Instagram, Brad Paisley called the donation ‘transformative’. “We just wanted to take a second and say it’s transformative, it will feed so many families, and what a way to start a marriage. I’m so excited,” the country star said.Kimberly said they were “so, so grateful”. She also pointed out that food insecurity was at a 10-year high in the Nashville area, making the timing “just so critical”. She added, “We’re just really grateful for your generosity.”Brown agreed: “What a wonderful thing to be thinking of others during such a chaotic time of wedding planning.”The donation was part of a larger charitable effort by Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce ahead of their wedding. According to the Associated Press, the couple donated a total of $26 million to 20 local and national charities. Swift's publicist said many of these organisations were based in places with which the couple has close connections. Nine of the charities were in New York, including Food Bank For NYC, City Harvest and Musical Mentors, a non-profit that connects music teachers with students who need support.The couple’s ties to Nashville are evident in their generous donation. The pop star has called Nashville one of her homes since she was a teenager. However, her gift to The Store is particularly close to her heart because of her relationship with the Paisleys. In 2007, when Swift was just 17 and promoting her debut album, she opened for Brad Paisley on his Bonfires and Amplifiers Tour. Nearly two decades later, the friendship remains strong. In fact, the Paisleys attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding.
Article Summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to 20 charities. One recipient was The Store, a Nashville non-profit fighting food insecurity. Rising food costs had forced the store to pause the admission of new families. Around 1,000 households were still waiting for help.

Article Title: ‘Injury much better now’: Neeraj Chopra on the path to recovery; to resume training and rehabilitation in next few weeks

Neeraj Chopra (PTI Photo)

New Delhi: Olympic and world champion javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra said his recovery from injury is on the right path and training, rehab process will begun in the next couple of weeks. The 2020 Tokyo Olympics gold medallist has kept next year as his target after sustaining an injury, with his focus on delivering strong performances ahead of LA 2028.Chopra, who won gold at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and silver at the Paris 2024 Olympics in men's javelin throw, has been one of India's leading figures in recent years. However, Chopra missed the recent 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya after he suffered an ankle ligament injury during a training session, which also ruled him out for the rest of the season."My injury is much better now. I faced some issues initially in the first month and a half, but it has improved significantly. I consulted Dr. Dinshaw Pardiwala and he has advised that I can now resume training and begin proper rehabilitation. My plan is to start both in the next couple of weeks," Neeraj told SAI Media.The two-time Olympic medallist clarified that he followed complete rest as advised by his medical team."For my injury, the doctors had advised rest, and that is exactly what I followed. With regard to competitions, TOPS (Target Olympic Podium Scheme) and SAI (Sports Authority of India) have been supporting me for years.I have been part of the TOPS Core Group for many years now, and whenever I need any support, they are there," he added.In Neeraj and Kishore Jena's absence, Yashvir Singh won a silver medal and Rohit Yadav a bronze in javelin throw at the 2026 Asian Games.Neeraj also welcomed the Union Cabinet's approval of the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme on October 28, calling it a major step for Indian sport."The Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme, which was approved by the Union Cabinet, is an amazing step. Athletes face a lot of issues in procuring certain equipment in India or have to import sporting equipment from abroad. With schemes like these, as equipment will be manufactured in India, it will become much easier for them to source it," he noted.He then went on to extend his best wishes to the Indian contingent for the upcoming Youth Olympic Games and added, "I wish all the best to the athletes heading to the Youth Olympics. Enjoy the experience and don't take too much pressure or get nervous. Whatever pressure you face at the Youth Olympics is good for you as it teaches you a lot. Use this opportunity to observe others and channel the pressure to your advantage, and I am sure you will do your best. "
Article Summary: Neeraj Chopra says his recovery from injury is on the right path. The 2020 Tokyo Olympics gold medallist has kept next year as his target. Chopra missed the recent 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya after he suffered an ankle ligament injury during a training session.

England head coach Brendon McCullum has backed Harry Brook 's leadership despite the team's failure to reach the final of the ODI tri-series in Pakistan. McCullum said the young captain had gained valuable experience from a difficult assignment.England lost their first three matches of the tournament before ending their campaign with a 55-run win over Sri Lanka in Lahore on Thursday. Brook's team looked set for another defeat after Pavan Rathnayake scored a century for Sri Lanka, but England fought back to bowl out their opponents for 331 while defending a target of 387."He (Brook) will have learned a lot from getting thrust into a situation like this where the game is travelling at breakneck speed, and you're having to make decisions which can win or lose a game," McCullum told Sky Sports, as quoted by Reuters.The 45-year-old praised Brook's understanding of the game and his ability to lead the team, adding that the batter had earned the respect of his teammates."He's one of the best tactical captains I've ever come across," McCullum said."He's got such an astute brain. He wears his intelligence lightly externally, but he's a very switched-on man and a very switched-on cricketer. He has the respect of the entire dressing room."He leads them. They follow him. He's interactive with his leadership. It's not just him out there on his own. He does call upon many other people as well."England will continue their preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup with a white-ball tour of Australia in November.Batter Jacob Bethell and fast bowler Jofra Archer are expected to return after missing the Pakistan tri-series. Former captain Jos Buttler, however, remains unavailable as he continues his recovery from hamstring surgery.

Article Title: 'We need to win both': Gautam Gambhir asks team India to win 'every match' of series

India spinner Varun Chakaravarthy said head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked the team to aim for a win in every match, even after sealing the five-match T20I series against New Zealand. With India having won the first three games, the spinner said the team was treating the remaining two matches as a separate series and wanted to win both.India entered the fourth T20I at Eden Park in Auckland after winning all three previous matches, with their batters leading the way. Abhishek Sharma led the chase with a 38-ball 113. Chakaravarthy said it would be difficult for the batters to better that performance, but hoped they could produce something similar.“I don't think you can top that, but I hope they can repeat that today. And yeah, they are used to playing in such pitches and such small venues. Yeah, so that played into our advantage for sure,” he said.Chakaravarthy, who is yet to play a match in the series, also spoke about the competition for places in the Indian team. He said players needed to keep working on their game and performing consistently, given the amount of talent available in Indian cricket.“Playing in India, the best thing that you want to happen for yourself is being in the contention. Article Title: Arshdeep Singh scripts history, becomes first Indian to 150 T20I wickets
Article Text:
India's Arshdeep Singh (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Most T20I wickets for India

Player Matches Wickets Economy Arshdeep Singh 103 150 8.66 Jasprit Bumrah 100 126 6.52 Axar Patel 116 116 7.76 Hardik Pandya 138 114 8.34

Arshdeep Singh etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, becoming the first Indian bowler to claim 150 wickets in the shortest format.The left-arm pacer reached the landmark in the final over of his spell when he dismissed New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner for five. Arshdeep bowled a full delivery outside off, forcing Santner to reach for the shot. The batter sliced it towards sweeper cover, where Nitish Kumar Reddy took a well-judged catch near the boundary.Arshdeep finished with his 150th T20I wicket in his 103rd match, further strengthening his position at the top of India's list of leading wicket-takers in the format.He has also reached the milestone in just 1,577 days since making his T20I debut, the quickest by any bowler. He surpassed Sri Lanka's Wanindu Hasaranga, who took 2,325 days to get to 150 wickets.Arshdeep is also among the quickest to the landmark in terms of deliveries bowled. He took 2,143 balls, behind Hasaranga (2,035), Rashid Khan (2,098) and Ehsan Khan (2,143). Among fast bowlers, the previous quickest was Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, who needed 2,532 deliveries.The achievement adds to a remarkable year for Arshdeep. With 40 T20I wickets in 2026, he has become the leading wicket-taker in a calendar year among players from Full Member nations. Ireland's Josh Little took 39 wickets in 2022, while Hasaranga claimed 38 in 2024 and Bhuvneshwar Kumar picked up 37 in 2022.Arshdeep's consistency has also been reflected in his economy rate. He has been India's leading T20I wicket-taker while maintaining an economy of 8.66.
Article Summary: Arshdeep Singh becomes first Indian bowler to claim 150 wickets in the shortest format. Left-arm pacer reached the landmark in the final over of his spell. He has also reached the milestone in just 1,577 days since making his T20I debut, the quickest by any bowler.
