Article Title: Mahatma Gandhi's grandson 30-acre Virginia land in US reclaimed after 20-month legal battle
Article Text:
Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.





SURAT: A US court has ordered a Virginia resident to remove his encroachment from land owned by the late Kanu Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson, and his wife Shiva Gandhi, after a 20-month legal battle led by Parimal Desai from Surat.The dispute involved 30 acres of land adjoining Shenandoah National Park in Warren County, Virginia, which the Gandhi couple bought in 1987. During their final years in South Gujarat, they created a charitable trust and transferred their assets to it. Desai now serves as managing trustee.Talking to TOI, Parimal Desai said, “It began when US national Gregory Black sent a legal notice to my residence on Jan 10, 2025. Black claimed the land by the adverse possession rule of Virginia, which allows a person to own land after 15 years of possession if five conditions are met. He ultimately could not prove his exclusive and actual possession condition and the ‘hostile claim’ condition.”Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi returned to India in 2013 and spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016. Under his will, his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi.In 2018, Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will. After her death in 2020, the will was executed and Desai took charge as managing trustee. The trust inherited her properties and financial assets to support its charitable activities.Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.“As I learnt about the land in Virginia, I went to the property in 2024 and got the survey done. If the trust wanted to do anything with land, it had to be in its possession. I got the will probated in a US court in 2025 and got the land title in the trust’s name,” he said.Black claimed he had occupied the land since 2008. In court he cited trails, a cabin, tree stands, a culvert and other improvements on the property, along with photographs from to support his claim.Desai said, “I had hired lawyers in the US and worked in India to win the claim. I used artificial intelligence (AI) to find the ways to contest the claim. When the final trial took place, from Sep 8 to 11, I told the court that Kanu Gandhi was Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson and he and his wife has donated the properties to the trust, which has the objective of propagating Gandhian philosophy.“We could prove with GIS maps that the cabin was not there for 15 years. I also went there many times since 2020 which disproved his claim of actual possession. We also found another woman residing on the land, which belied Black’s claim that he had exclusive possession.”In the order dated Oct 21, Judge Daryl L. Funk of the Warren County Circuit Court ruled in favour of Desai and the trust. The court directed Black to pay $11,375 towards the fees of the Guardian ad Litem representing unknown heirs.The court also ordered Black to remove the cabin, hunting stands, hunting huts and personal belongings from the property within 30 days at his own expense. Black was directed to surrender possession of the land and cease entering or exercising any ownership rights over it.
Article Summary: Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016 and his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi. Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will in 2020. Parimal Desai took charge as managing trustee.

Article Title: '1st we lost our land, now compensation': Money from PNB’s Greater Noida branch accounts diverted to 6 accounts in Goa, Mumbai, Jharkhand
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery

TOI

‘First we lost our land & now our compensation’

TOI





NOIDA: Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand, police have found in their investigation into alleged embezzlement of Rs 35 crore from the branch. Police have frozen the accounts.The police cybercrime team and PNB’s vigilance team, investigating the alleged fraud, said the money didn’t stay in these accounts and have been routed to others. Investigators suspect that branch employees and the bank manager may have come into contact with a cyberfraud gang and allegedly facilitated the irregularities.So far, 30 account holders from Aichhar, Birondi, Bironda, Kyampur and several other neighbouring villages have submitted complaints at Beta 2 police station. The SHO said 12 fresh complaints were filed on Thursday and all the complaints were being clubbed into an FIR filed earlier under BNS Section 316(5) (criminal breach of trust) against the PNB branch staffers.The FIR was lodged on Wednesday after Shrichand, a resident of Viroondi Chakrasenpur village in Surajpur, alleged that Rs 1.16 crore was embezzled from his FD linked to his account at the Aichhar branch.On Thursday, several account holders staged a protest outside the Aichhar branch, with several claiming that gold and silver jewellery and other valuables have gone missing from lockers too.In some cases, these have been replaced with faux ornaments.Some accused bank officials of altering registered mobile numbers and email IDs before diverting money from fixed deposits (FDs) and savings accounts to ensure that account holders did not receive transaction alerts. Many complainants, most of them farmers who had received land compensation from Noida Authority, said their accounts were completely emptied out by the bank staff.Ajipal, a resident of Birondi village, toldthat he received compensation after his family’s land was acquired in 2001 and rented a locker at the bank in 2014. He said he learnt of the alleged fraud on Oct 27 and approached the bank for details on a Rs 35.34 lakh fixed deposit (FD) and 18 tolas (approximately 210 grams) of gold and 1 kg of silver jewellery in his locker, but the bank manager did not give a clear response. He alleged that the mobile number and email ID registered against his account did not match his actual contact details and may have been deliberately changed to stop him from receiving alerts about unauthorised transactions.“On Thursday, bank staffers were asking affected customers to submit affidavits detailing the money held in their fixed deposits (FDs) and the gold and silver jewellery kept in their lockers,” Ajipal said. While the process is meant to document their claims, several account holders said they were still awaiting clear answers about the status of their money and jewellery.Santosh, a resident from Birondi village, alleged that Rs 1.3 crore had been deposited in her bank account as land acquisition compensation, of which Rs 1.2 crore had allegedly gone missing. Expressing anguish over the alleged loss, she said her family had already lost its land to acquisition and had deposited the compensation money in the bank with the expectation that it would secure their future. “First, they took our land, and now the bank has taken away our compensation money,” she said.Meanwhile, senior bank officials from Mumbai and Noida, who have been called in to monitor the case, toldthat audits have been ordered at other branches in Gautam Budh Nagar where land acquisition compensation was deposited over the past two years. Rajesh Bhowmik, the bank’s zonal manager, said a case had been registered with the CBI. Money of three account holders has been credited to their accounts, he said. “…three claims amounting to Rs 43 lakh had been settled as of yesterday (Wednesday). The bank assures its customers that all genuine claims will be honoured,” PNB said in a statement.On Wednesday, PNB suspended the branch manager and four other employees. Bhowmik said the bank will examine each account holder’s case individually before refunding the amounts.“PNB has taken serious cognisance of the complaints regarding alleged financial irregularities involving certain customer fixed/ savings bank deposit accounts at its Greater Noida branch. The matter is being examined on priority, and the bank is extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and is taking necessary steps to verify the facts, assess the extent of the reported discrepancies and address the concerns of affected customers,” the bank said in a statement.
Article Summary: 30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery. Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand. Police have frozen the accounts.

Article Title: BJP loses Darbhanga MLC seat to RJD in final stage of counting
Article Text:
RJD’s Anil Kumar Jha (right), who won Darbhanga Graduates’ seat, with party national working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav





PATNA: The opposition RJD on Thursday won the Darbhanga Graduates’ constituency of the Bihar legislative council with its candidate Anil Kumar Jha defeating sitting MLC and BJP nominee Sarvesh Kumar after a dramatic shift in preferential votes during the final stage of counting.Officials at the counting centre at Khel Bhawan in Darbhanga told TOI Jha was declared elected after taking a lead of 533 votes over Kumar at the end of the 39th round, following the elimination of 38 candidates. A total of 40 candidates contested the seat, where polling was held on Oct 23.Darbhanga divisional commissioner-cum-returning officer Himanshu Kumar Rai told TOI over the phone Jha was declared elected on Thursday after completion of all formalities and receipt of the necessary approval from the Election Commission Until the end of the 38th round, the BJP candidate was ahead. Kumar had secured 20,033 votes, while Jha had polled 19,029, giving the BJP nominee a lead of 1,004 votes. The result changed in the 39th round after Mohammad Imtiyaz Noorani of Jan Suraaj, the third-leading candidate, was eliminated.Officials said voters who had marked Noorani as their first preference had also indicated second preferences for Kumar and Jha.Of these transferable votes, 2,900 went to Jha, while 1,363 were added to Kumar’s tally. The transfer gave Jha the decisive lead. With only the two leading candidates remaining in the count, the returning officer declared Jha elected.Kumar congratulated Jha at the counting centre soon after the result became clear.The outcome revised the final tally for the eight teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies that went to polls on Oct 23. The BJP won two seats, the RJD two, the JD(U) one, Jan Suraaj one and Independents two.BJP functionaries had on Wednesday claimed Kumar had retained the Darbhanga Graduates’ seat. However, counting continued till Thursday evening when the preference transfers altered the result.Reacting to the victory, RJD national working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav said the Darbhanga Graduates’ verdict was “the educated society’s open mandate against the NDA govt’s corruption, abuse of power, BJP’s repressive action against teachers and youth, and the NDA’s anti-people policies.”
Article Summary: Opposition RJD wins Darbhanga Graduates’ constituency of Bihar legislative council. RJD candidate Anil Kumar Jha defeated sitting MLC and BJP nominee Sarvesh Kumar after a dramatic shift in preferential votes during the final stage of counting.

Article Title: Husband stabs wife over 150 times with scissors and knife on Karwa Chauth
Article Text:
Victim-Nikita Kumari (Image-Social Media)





ARA: In a bone-chilling incident of domestic violence in the Town police station area of Ara on Thursday, a man stabbed his wife more than 150 times, leaving her critically injured.Describing the gruesome incident to TOI on Friday, renowned Ara surgeon Dr Vikash Singh, more popularly known as the 'Goliya Wala Doctor' for his expertise in operating on gunshot victims who come to him from across the Shahabad region, said, "The injured woman has undergone more than 150 stitches as she was stabbed very badly all over her body. On her neck and the surrounding area alone, there were more than 70 stab wounds, 30 to 40 wounds on her back and about 15 to 20 wounds near her breast/chest. I have rarely come across such gruesome stabbing injuries in any patient. It took me more than three hours of surgery to save her life. She is being kept under constant observation."The surgeon added, "Saving her life was very challenging. She needed O-negative blood, which is extremely rare to find immediately. However, we somehow managed to procure O-negative blood for transfusion, as she had suffered profuse bleeding after being severely stabbed.It is by the grace of God that she has survived such a gruesome attack."The doctor added that the victim was first rushed to Sadar Hospital in Ara. However, after doctors there referred her to Patna, her family members brought her to his private clinic in Ara, where she is currently undergoing treatment.Meanwhile, the Bhojpur SP's office, in a press release on Friday afternoon, stated, "The accused, identified as Pankaj Kumar Thakur, son of Radha Mohan Thakur and a resident of Bhakura village under the Ara Mufassil police station area, has been arrested. As per the preliminary investigation, his intention behind the severe stabbing with scissors and a knife was to kill his wife, Nikita Kumari. The accused has been sent to jail. An FIR has been lodged at Ara Town police station based on the statement of the victim woman's family members."Speaking to the media, the victim's father, Manoj Kumar Thakur, said, "My daughter was married to the accused, Pankaj Kumar Thakur, about six years ago. Six months after the marriage, Pankaj started beating my daughter without any reason. I used to call the Dial 112 police team whenever he harassed my daughter. However, keeping my daughter's married life in mind, I spared him from legal action. But I didn't know that one day he would turn so brutal. "The victim's aunt, Usha Devi, claimed that the accused sat astride his wife while she was asleep and stabbed her repeatedly in a gruesome manner."She has two small children, a son and a daughter. May she survive to bring them up," the victim's aunt said, crying inconsolably at the hospital.
Article Summary: A man stabbed his wife more than 150 times, leaving her critically injured. Accused, Pankaj Kumar Thakur, has been arrested and sent to jail. The victim's aunt claimed that the accused sat astride his wife while she was asleep and stabbed her repeatedly.

Great leveller: Facing a random trivia set is a brave act of putting yourself out there, to locate your threshold of comfort, to understand the limits to which you can push your amygdala – are you the fight geek or the flight geek? How much does it take to spook you?

- Inputs by Mudita Chauhan-Mubayi





Beyond spooky decor, cliched drink names and costume parties, Delhi is embracing a more interactive way to celebrate Halloween this year. From horror movie trivia to rounds on spooky characters, themed quizzes are bringing a dose of friendly competition to the city’s nightlife. After all, a ticking quiz timer can be just as nerve-racking as a horror film!Halloween is all about winning, with your costume, decor, number of candies at trick-or-treat, and now, the points on your quiz scoreboard. “The flavour of questions in such quizzes is quite interesting. The potential to have innovative rounds is immense. Like a play on trick or treat or an identification round of ghosts/ghastly figures called Boo Am I?,” notes Sumantra Sarathi Datta, convenor of Delhi Quiz Club.While Gen Z is more keen on Halloween-themed experiences, it goes beyond a specific demographic. Sanjali Nirwani, founder of a Gurgaon-based bar which hosts regular game nights, adds, “Games, costumes and a little friendly competition are things people across age groups can enjoy. It’s an experience that works just as well for regulars as it does for first-time visitors.”Arvind Nair, quizmaster and founder of Quriosity shares that a niche quiz makes niche info and titbits surprisingly useful. “You might come thinking you’re great at horror movies, only to find your teammate knows all the answers on music or pop culture. Someone at your table will know something obscure that they never thought would be of any use, and this flex somehow brings the whole table together,” he says.Mudita Chauhan-Mubayi, founder-director of Quizcraft Global, says, “As a quizmaker, I get to watch hundreds of quizzes up close. Thrills, chills, spills, kills... frankly, the drama is no less than watching a film in the thriller/ horror/suspense genre! I feel the perceived physical threat of a movie monster jumping out at you is much like the ‘existential’ threat of a quiz timer closing in on you, tick-tock, tick-tock!”Halloween celebrations move beyond just pictures and find an experiential way to mark the spooky festivities. Arvind, who recently planned a Halloween-themed quiz, said, “I’ve always wanted quizzing to be about more than just knowing the right answers. It’s about bringing people together, discovering things and having a great night out. Halloween felt like a natural fit because of the possible range of questions from pop culture, movies and music. And as always, a little friendly competition.”The theme is also popular at the city’s game nights. Sanjali shares, “Game nights are becoming a fresh way to celebrate the festival in the city. While Halloween is often associated with costume parties and nightlife, we’re bringing a more interactive element to it. It’s an opportunity to dress up, solve a themed mystery, and connect with people beyond the usual party setting.”
Article Summary: Halloween celebrations move beyond just pictures and find an experiential way to mark the spooky festivities. From horror movie trivia to rounds on spooky characters, themed quizzes are bringing a dose of friendly competition to the city’s nightlife.

Article Title: Theatre Review: Death and the Maiden: When justice fails, who gets to decide the truth?
Article Text:
Death and the Maiden (

Psychological Thriller

)

Rating: 3 stars

Directed by: Bruce Guthrie

Cast: Ira Dubey , Vivek Gomber, Neil Bhoopalam

Language: English

Duration: 120 minutes

Should you watch it?





While some plays entertain you, there are others that leave you with questions you cannot quite shake off. Bruce Guthrie’s Death and the Maiden, featuring Ira Dubey, Neil Bhoopalam and Vivek Gomber, belongs to the latter category and its definitely not your easy evening at the theatre. The play’s greatest strength lies in the moral unease it creates, though its ambiguity may leave some viewers seeking greater emotional resolution. But perhaps that unresolved feeling is the point. Sometimes, the most powerful theatre does not tell us what to think; it makes us confront what we would rather not think about.Based on Chilean playwright Ariel Dorfman’s acclaimed play, this psychological thriller explores the uncomfortable intersection of trauma, memory, justice and revenge. Set in an unnamed country emerging from dictatorship, the story centres on Paulina Escobar, née Salas, a former political prisoner who believes that a stranger her husband brings home to their beach house is the man who blindfolded, tortured and raped her for days, 15 years ago.What follows is not merely a confrontation between three individuals, but a deeply unsettling examination of what happens when the pursuit of justice collides with the limitations of the law.As Paulina, Ira carries the emotional weight of the play, portraying a woman whose past refuses to remain in the past, capturing the rage, vulnerability and psychological turmoil of someone who has endured unimaginable trauma. Paulina is not a character whose actions are easy to agree with at every turn, but that is precisely what makes her compelling. Her desperation for justice forces the audience to confront an uncomfortable question: when a survivor’s voice goes unheard, what recourse does she have?Neil brings an intriguing unpredictability to Roberto Miranda, the man at the centre of Paulina’s accusations. His performance sustains the uncertainty that drives the narrative. Is he guilty? Is Paulina certain because she remembers him, or does trauma complicate the reliability of memory? Neil keeps these questions alive, preventing the audience from settling too comfortably on either side. Vivek, as Paulina’s husband, Gerardo, occupies the difficult middle ground between personal loyalty and the principles of justice. His character embodies the moral and legal dilemma at the heart of the play: what does one do when the person one loves demands justice, but the evidence is far from straightforward?Bruce's direction understands the power of restraint. The tightly focused setting, atmospheric lighting and sound create a sense of confinement that mirrors the characters’ psychological entrapment. And the music plays a crucial role as Paulina recalls that during her torture, the doctor played Franz Schubert’s String Quartet No. 14 in D minor, known as Death and the Maiden. The composition, which lends the play its title, becomes an unsettling reminder of her suffering. What might otherwise be a beautiful piece of classical music is inextricably linked to the horror of her memories, turning it into a haunting presence in the narrative.The play’s strength lies in its refusal to offer easy answers. However, its emotionally demanding subject and dense psychological exchanges may not appeal to audiences looking for a fast-paced thriller with a neat resolution. This is theatre that requires patience and a willingness to sit with discomfort.Ultimately, Death and the Maiden leaves you grappling with questions of institutional accountability. Can a society truly move forward without confronting the violence of its past? Is forgiveness possible without justice? And when formal systems fail survivors, how far can an individual go in seeking redress before justice becomes vengeance?The play does not hand its audience a verdict. Instead, it places us in the uncomfortable position of having to arrive at one, even as it challenges the certainty of our own judgement. And that is what makes this production linger in the mind long after the curtain falls.Yes, for its gripping performances and unsettling exploration of trauma, memory and justice, that leaves you questioning how far one can go in the pursuit of truth.
Article Summary: Based on Chilean playwright Ariel Dorfman’s acclaimed play, this psychological thriller explores the uncomfortable intersection of trauma, memory, justice and revenge. Set in an unnamed country emerging from dictatorship, the story centres on Paulina Escobar, née Salas, a former political prisoner who believes that a stranger her husband brings home to their beach house is the man who blindfolded, tortured and raped her for days, 15 years ago.

Article Title: Mumbai’s Halloween game gets spookier

Ghost walks and paranormal encounters

Drinks, costumes and clubbing

Article Title: Blame game erupts in Mahayuti after it secures only two of the five seats in Maharashtra MLC elections; MVA wins 3 constituencies
Article Text:
Mumbai/Pune/Nagpur:





Knives were out within Mahayuti after the governing coalition managed to bag only two of the five seats in the MLC elections in Maharashtra, while MVA secured three.The wins for the opposition bloc were touted as a big turnaround after the 2024 assembly poll drubbing. BJP contested three seats but managed to bag only one. Shiv Sena fought from two and won one. NCP failed to even open its account.The biggest embarrassment for BJP was in Nagpur—CM Devendra Fadnavis ’s home turf and RSS’s citadel—where its loss seemed to be a result of an internal rift within the party. Congress scored its sole win there from polls in three states, when its candidate, Abhijit Wanjarri, secured a second consecutive term and defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes in a nail-biting finish that went beyond 41 hours of counting.Within hours of the results, a blame game erupted in Mahayuti, with BJP and Sena accusing each other of failing to support allies and refusing to rein in rebels in the fray.In the run-up to the polls, the Pune seats became a bone of contention in Mahayuti. BJP decided to contest both graduates and teachers constituencies despite Sena staking its claim to them. Instead of backing BJP, Sena supported rebels from its own party.After deliberations, Sena rebel Mangesh Chivte withdrew from the graduates contest, while another, Sachin Sanap, continued to challenge BJP’s Kaustubh Gawade. Although Gawade managed to snatch a victory, BJP on Thursday expressed disappointment over Sena’s stand.State cabinet minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule from BJP said senior alliance members would review the results and “track down who played spoilsport”, while party spokesperson Navnath Ban said Sena failed to uphold the alliance’s principles by refusing to cooperate with BJP and NCP. “Mahayuti, otherwise, would have won all five MLC seats,” he asserted.State BJP vice-president Keshav Upadhye said while there was a need for introspection, he blamed allies for his party’s defeat. “The results are not proof of the opposition’s success but evidence of the deeds of some ‘well-wishers’ within Mahayuti,” he posted.Sanjay Kute, BJP MLA, said BJP had worked sincerely for Shiv Sena’s Amravati graduate constituency candidate, Kiran Sarnaik, who won. “We expelled all those who stood as rebels against the Sena candidate. On the other hand, Sena is yet to expel its rebel candidate, Shrikant Deshpande. BJP worked closely with Sena in Amravati to ensure its victory,” he said.In the Aurangabad graduates constituency, the two NCP factions were directly pitted against each other, but NCP got no support from Sena despite it having a strong presence in the Marathwada region. Senior Sena functionary Abdul Sattar acknowledged that he backed the NCP (SP) candidate, Pratapsinh Patil, instead of Satish Chavan from NCP, but criticised NCP for having nominated Chavan in the first place and asked the party to introspect. “In previous elections, our party workers supported the Mahayuti candidate. However, this time, the candidate selection was wrong. So, we did not campaign for him,” he said.A BJP functionary said in Pune, Sena workers openly campaigned against BJP nominee Smita Jadhav in the graduates constituency. “Had Mahayuti contested unitedly, we would have won all five seats.” Ravindra Dhangekar, Pune Sena chief and former MLA, hit back, calling the results a reality check for BJP. “BJP should stop taking its alliance partners for granted,” he said.The biggest setback for BJP came in its stronghold of Nagpur. The outcome put the party’s candidate selection under scrutiny. Former MLC Anil Sole, a Gadkari confidant who was denied a ticket, entered the fray as an Independent. He agreed to stop campaigning only after Fadnavis visited his home to address the dispute. The extent to which the rebellion affected Kohale’s prospects remains unclear. But more than 15,000 votes were declared invalid, including nearly 9,000 ballots reportedly marked with the number ‘2’ against Kohale, without preferences for the other 37 candidates. The unusually high number prompted questions about whether ballots reflected voter error or dissatisfaction over candidate selection. Kohale said he would appeal against invalid votes.NCP was restrained in its response to its loss and the lack of support from allies. Party chief Sunetra Pawar said, “Winning and losing are part of every election, but every outcome is a lesson.” Backing party colleague Praful Patel’s call for introspection, NCP minister Chhagan Bhujbal said the results called for an “honest and rigorous self-assessment” by Mahayuti and his own party. He said educated and politically aware voters were moving away from NCP and their views could influence a wider section of the public. He said the alliance must examine where it went wrong and take corrective measures.
Article Summary: Opposition wins touted as a big turnaround after the 2024 assembly poll drubbing. BJP contested three seats but managed to bag only one. Shiv Sena fought from two and won one. NCP failed to even open its account. The biggest embarrassment for BJP was in Nagpur.

Article Title: Sharad Pawar’s last-minute pick caused major upset in Marathwada MLC poll
Article Text:
NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil (C) after winning Aurangabad graduate constituency poll on Thursday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





NCP (SP) candidate Dr Pratapsinh Patil defeated sitting MLC Satish Chavan, ending the latter’s uninterrupted 18-year hold over the Aurangabad Graduates’ constituency. Patil polled 85,876 votes and defeated the Ajit Pawar-led NCP candidate by 18,124 votes after a marathon 45-hour count.The victory capped a campaign built around anti-incumbency, unemployed youth, rising education costs and anger among graduates who felt neglected after nearly two decades of the same representation. The outcome was also a gamble that paid off for Sharad Pawar . The NCP (SP) chief was initially inclined to field senior politician Rajesh Tope. However, Tope persuaded the party to give the ticket to Patil and then mobilised the organisation across all 76 talukas of Marathwada.Patil entered the race late and got barely two weeks to campaign. “I got only 12 to 15 days. We covered all 76 talukas and took our issues directly to graduates,” Patil said.The campaign focused less on voter registration and more on voter anger. The party aggressively raised issues of unemployment, inflation and rising educational expenses, while targeting Chavan’s long incumbency. NCP (SP) netas Supriya Sule and Rohit Pawar campaigned extensively, while the party also reached out to major educational institutions across the region.“I decided not to criticise my rival. I focused on my agenda and vision. Graduate voters from Marathwada were taken for granted and they vented their anger through the ballot boxes,” Patil said.He claimed the mood against the incumbent was visible even during counting. “Angry voters even left chits inside ballot boxes. One read: ‘Satish, bro, it is done now’,” Patil said.The result was aided by cross-voting and discontent within Mahayuti. Shiv Sena MLA Abdul Sattar openly backed Patil, while sections of BJP and Sena workers reportedly drifted away from the Mahayuti candidate.Patil is the brother of Parbhani Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Rahul Patil and cousin of Georai MLA Vijaysinh Pandit.For Chavan, the defeat marks the end of an 18-year run in a constituency he had dominated since 2008. Accepting the verdict, the outgoing MLC struck a conciliatory note. “The people’s decision is final in democracy. I will continue working for jobs and industry for Marathwada’s youth. Do not be dejected by defeat, nor carried away by victory,” Chavan said.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) candidate Dr Pratapsinh Patil defeated sitting MLC Satish Chavan, ending the latter’s uninterrupted 18-year hold over the Aurangabad Graduates’ constituency. Patil polled 85,876 votes and defeated the Ajit Pawar-led NCP candidate by 18,124 votes.

Article Title: ​NCP (SP) candidate nears Aurangabad graduate poll win; anti-incumbency, spirited campaign by rival camp hit NCP
Article Text:
NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil (centre) with supporters at the counting centre on Wednesday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil moved closer to victory in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election on Wednesday, opening a sizeable lead over NCP’s three-term MLC Satish Chavan as counting continued on the second day.With counting of ballot papers still underway late on Wednesday, Patil had secured 73,931 first-preference votes, ahead of Chavan’s 60,768. The victory quota was fixed at 88,558 votes, forcing the contest into the second-preference count as no candidate crossed the required mark.Though the final result was awaited, NCP (SP) workers began celebrations, treating Patil’s lead as decisive.“This victory is not mine alone. This victory belongs to every graduate who showed faith in me to ask the questions of our future, to fight for our rights, and to usher in a new era of education, employment, and development. This victory belongs to that youth whose eyes hold dreams, to those students who seek quality education and employment opportunities, as well as to all teachers, educated citizens, and every individual who harbors the expectation of change,” Patil said.Political observers attributed Chavan’s likely defeat to strong anti-incumbency and an aggressive campaign by NCP (SP). Several graduate voters had expressed dissatisfaction over Chavan’s alleged lack of accessibility and silence on key issues.His perceived overconfidence and strained relations with sections of Mahayuti politicians were also cited as factors.Shiv Sena MLA Abdul Sattar openly campaigned against Chavan, while some disgruntled BJP and Mahayuti functionaries were believed to have tacitly backed Patil.Patil, meanwhile, ran a tightly coordinated campaign with support from his brother, Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Rahul Patil, and senior NCP (SP) netas including Supriya Sule , Rohit Pawar, Rajesh Tope and Shashikant Shinde. His campaign focused on issues such as unemployment among graduates, contractual teachers and health insurance, while avoiding personal attacks on rivals.Among the 41 candidates in the fray, independent reel-star Raviraj Sabale finished third with more than 19,000 first-preference votes.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil moved closer to victory in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election on Wednesday. Patil had secured 73,931 first- preference votes, ahead of Satish Chavan’s 60,768.

Article Title: High invalid votes from graduates is yet another stark story of MLC polls, tradition continues
Article Text:
Kolhapur:

Scribblings on ballot papers steal the show





The graduates’ and teachers’ legislative council elections are notorious for the high number of invalid votes, despite the expectation that these educated voters would take care while marking their ballot papers.Election authorities, political parties and candidates repeatedly explain the dos and don’ts, yet a substantial number of ballots continue to be rejected. In the Pune division graduates’ constituency, 17,299 votes were declared invalid, while Nagpur graduates recorded 15,302 invalid votes and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 11,783.In these graduates’ constituencies, the number of invalid votes exceeded the gap between the first-preference votes secured by the leading and second-placed candidates, highlighting their potential significance in determining the outcome.The teachers’ constituencies also recorded invalid votes, with 1,673 ballots rejected in Pune and 627 in Amravati. At the beginning of counting, officials first count the ballot papers and determine how many are valid and invalid. They then calculate the winning quota—the number of valid votes a candidate must secure to be elected.These MLC elections follow a preferential voting system in which votes can be transferred according to voters’ marked preferences.Voters indicate their choices using the numerals 1, 2, 3 and so on. To help voters avoid mistakes, parties stressed that the first preference could be marked with a simple vertical stroke representing the numeral “1”, without touching the borders of the designated box. Despite these repeated instructions, large numbers of ballots were still declared invalid.Sunil Modi, Shiv Sena (UBT) candidate for Pune graduates’ seat and a co-opted corporator in Kolhapur Municipal Corporation, said invalid votes typically accounted for 8% to 10% in MLC elections in Maharashtra and other states.“We observed that voters give repetitive same preference for different candidates, there is some overwriting, some give tick marks, some write numbers such that the numeral cannot be recognized as per the given patterns. There always has been 8 to 10% such invalid votes in MLC elections not just in Maharashtra but in other states also.”According to political experts, the preferential voting system is meant for those people who are literate and can understand wholly the value of their vote.“This system was brought in exclusively for the graduates and teachers who could understand the system properly. A wise voter can give preference to all candidates as at least one of his votes of any preference can bear some value in the results. Unfortunately neither the candidates nor the voters know about the system. One mistake or a simple overwriting can make the vote invalid and the candidates will hurt eventually,” Ravindra Bhanage, professor of political science at Shivaji University, Kolhapur, said.“Since these elections are held once in six years, all stakeholders should take efforts at least from months before so that the voters are trained to cast valid votes,” said Bhanage.“The voters should realise that the winning quota of votes is determined only on the basis of valid votes. It should be imbibed in the mind of voters that one of their preferences may be useful in the end and get a clear mandate,” added the professor.More than the winners and losers, it was the messages scribbled on ballot papers that became a talking point during the two-day counting of votes for the Aurangabad graduates’ constituency, which continued until Wednesday.As ballot boxes were opened at the Chikalthana counting centre, officials found not just the prescribed preference markings, but also expressions of anger, sarcasm and despair.“Will never forgive those who change parties like clothes,” one voter wrote, expressing resentment over party-hopping. The remark appeared to target NCP candidate Satish Chavan, who had left the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction after his defeat in the 2024 assembly elections.Another ballot carried the message, “You did not even make an attempt to become our voice,” reflecting dissatisfaction with the elected representative’s performance.Frustration over unemployment also found expression, with one voter writing, “Did my degree, now I regret it!”Chavan, who has represented the constituency three times, also faced pointed remarks. “Satish, it’s done bro!” read a message found on a few ballot papers.Election authorities said names, signatures, slogans, symbols or messages that violate ballot secrecy render a vote invalid under the Conduct of Election Rules.Over 16,000 ballot papers were declared invalid during counting. “Besides those bearing messages, many were rejected because voters had failed to follow the prescribed rules for marking their preferences,” authorities said.
Article Summary: In Pune division graduates’ constituency, 17,299 votes were declared invalid. Nagpur graduates recorded 15,302 invalid votes and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 11,783. In teachers’ constituencies also recorded invalid votes, with 1,673 ballots rejected in Pune and 627 in Amravati.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: BJP, Sena spar after MVA wins in Pune, Nagpur, Aurangabad
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





PUNE/NAGPUR: Knives are out within Mahayuti after the ruling coalition managed to win only two of the five seats in the Maharashtra Legislative Council (MLC) elections, while Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) secured victory in three — touted as a big turnaround after the assembly poll drubbing.The biggest embarrassment for BJP was in Nagpur graduates constituency, where Congress’ Abhijit Wanjarri secured a second consecutive term, defeating party nominee Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes in a nail-biting finish that went beyond 41 hours of counting. While Wanjarri was the lone Congress warrior to win an MLC election across India, he also trounced his rival in the RSS citadel and home turf of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, despite the senior leadership in the vanguard of the campaign and its mammoth organisational machinery in place.Wanjarri told reporters after his victory he used “brains against BJP’s might”. The result surprised BJP circles, where confidence in Kohale’s prospects had persisted even as fortunes oscillated during counting.Within hours of the results, a blame game played out between BJP and its ally Shiv Sena, with both parties accusing each other of failing to support alliance candidates. BJP contested three seats, including Pune graduates and teachers constituencies and Nagpur graduates seat, but managed to bag only the Pune graduates’ seat.A day after counting, senior BJP leader and cabinet minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said senior alliance members would review the results. “We will track down who played spoilsport. Corrective measures will be taken,” he said.In the run-up to polls, the MLC seats in Pune division became a bone of contention between Mahayuti allies with BJP contesting both graduates and teachers’ constituencies, despite Shinde-Sena staking its claim to twin seats. Instead of backing its ally, Sena supported rebels from its own party against BJP nominees. After deliberations, Sena rebel Mangesh Chivte withdrew from the graduates’ constituency contest, while another, Sachin Sanap, continued to challenge BJP’s Kaustubh Gawade. Although Gawade managed to snatch a victory, BJP on Thursday expressed disappointment over Shiv Sena’s stand.A BJP leader said, “While in the teachers’ constituency, Sena supported a rebel candidate, in the graduates’ constituency, its workers openly campaigned against our candidate, Smita Jadhav, and we lost. Had Mahayuti contested unitedly, we would have won all five seats.” Sena hit back at BJP. Former MLA and Pune unit chief Ravindra Dhangekar said, “The results show BJP should stop taking its alliance partners for granted. The verdict has come as a reality check for BJP.”The contest in Aurangabad graduates’ constituency too turned into a battle between the two factions of Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). However, Sunetra Pawar’s faction did not receive support from its ally, Shiv Sena, which has a strong presence in the Marathwada region.NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil defeated NCP’s Satish Chavan. Following the results, senior Sena leader Abdul Sattar admitted on Thursday he backed Sharad Pawar’s candidate instead of his alliance partner’s nominee. Sattar criticised NCP for nominating Chavan and said the party should introspect.“In previous elections, our party workers supported the Mahayuti candidate. However, this time, the candidate selection was wrong, so we did not campaign for him. The results also reveal that educated voters are moving away from us, and we need to take corrective measures,” Sattar said. With the defeat in the Aurangabad seat, NCP failed to open its account. Party chief Sunetra Pawar said, “Winning and losing are part of every election, but every outcome is a lesson. ”The biggest setback for BJP came in its stronghold of Nagpur. The outcome has put BJP’s candidate selection under scrutiny. Former MLC Anil Sole, a Gadkari confidante who was denied a ticket, entered the fray as an Independent. He agreed to stop campaigning only after Fadnavis visited his home to address the dispute.The extent to which the rebellion affected Kohale’s prospects remains unclear. But, more than 15,000 votes were declared invalid, including nearly 9,000 ballots reportedly marked with the number ‘2’ against Kohale but without preferences for other 37 candidates. The unusually high number has prompted questions about whether ballots reflected voter error or dissatisfaction over candidate selection. Kohale has said he would appeal against invalid votes.Besides being the home turf of Fadnavis and Gadkari, who represented the graduates’ constituency from 1990 to 2014, BJP’s attempt to reclaim the seat was therefore tied to its political legacy in the region as well as its organisational strength.“Nagpur and Pune were prestigious seats for us. I was in charge of Nagpur, but unfortunately, we still fell short. I take responsibility for the defeat in Nagpur. We will ensure we win the seat in the next elections,” said Bawankule.
Article Summary: Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) secured victory in three seats. The biggest embarrassment for BJP was in Nagpur graduates constituency. Congress’ Abhijit Wanjarri secured a second consecutive term. BJP and Shiv Sena accuse each other of failing to support alliance candidates.
